title: Kernel Probing & Workload Synthesis Notebook
body:
Purpose:
This notebook records the design and experiment plan for a lightweight runtime benchmarking harness focused on kernel probing and synthetic workload generation. Goal is to create repeatable microbenchmarks and trace-driven synthesis that exercise
- kernel selection and fallback paths,
- KV cache behavior under prefix churn,
- scheduler/pack/unpack latency under real-ish mix of requests.

Scope and constraints:
- NOT an e2e perf lab (that's coverage of other docs). This is intentionally compact and automatable: single-binary harness + trace generator + small reporting dashboard.
- Must run in CI (emulated GPU if needed) and on dedicated perf lane GPUs.
- Emphasize reproducibility: seedable workload generator, snapshot of model weights/quant config, deterministic sampling where possible.

Principles:
- Probe kernels in isolation (single-op hot loops) and in integration (request-serving path).
- Keep signal-to-noise high: control host CPU load, repeat runs, clear preconditions for KV state.
- Make regressions actionable: measure microsignals (kernel selection rate, kv hit ratio, ephemeral memory spikes) not just p95 tokens.

High-level architecture:
- harnessctl (CLI) spawns target runtime with instrumentation hooks (trace socket).
- trace-synth (python) consumes real trace samples and generates parameterized workloads (session lengths, prefix reuse, insert/evict patterns).
- microprobe (C++) does single-kernel tight loops with perf counters and cuda profiling enabled.
- aggregator uploads JSON summaries to perf-store (S3) and computes deltas vs baseline.

Trace Synthesis approach:
- Input: collection of production traces (sanitized) and synthetic knobs.
- Synthesis model: Markov session generator seeded by empirical session-length distribution and prompt-topics. Each session has: initial prefix (0..N tokens), interactive turns (Poisson with lambda tuned to prod), and random continuation length.
- KV churn model: configurable parameters: prefix_reuse_prob, prefix_eviction_window, kv_shard_skew. We emulate localities: 60% hot prefixes, 30% warm, 10% cold.
- Timing jitter: inter-arrival distributions modeled as exponential+burst (to surface batching interactions).
- Output: workload manifest (JSON list) consumed by harnessctl; also a compact binary trace format for microprobe replay.

Microbench matrix (planned):
- Kernel microprobe: single-kernel run across seq_len=[8,64,512], batch=[1,4,16], dtype=[fp16,int8,q4]. Measure: latency per step, kernel occupancy, memory bandwidth.
- KV cache microprobe: prefix lookup latency under: hot-only, uniform random, tail-heavy. Measure: lookup p50/p95, insert latency, eviction rate.
- Scheduler packing: variable concurrent requests (1..128), small/large token distributions. Measure: pack latency, expected vs actual batch sizes, starvation events.
- Integrated scenario: trace-synth workload with KV churn + model variants; measure overall p50/p95/p99, kernel selection distribution, cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, and GC pauses.

Benchmark protocols and repeatability:
- Warmup: always run 3 warmup iterations before measurement; warmup traces use same seed but flagged separately.
- Repeats: 10 measurement iterations per cell, compute median and 95% bootstrap CI.
- Environment pinning: CUDA driver, kernel module versions logged; set POWERLIMIT and CPU governor to eliminate host variability.
- Artifacts recorded: harness stdout/stderr, nvprof/nvmetrics snapshot, perf counters, kernel selection trace, KV state dump (first/last 100 keys).

Regression detection heuristics:
- Primary triggers (automatic):
  - regression if change in p95 latency >= 10% relative and p-value < 0.05 (Mann-Whitney U test across iterations).
  - kernel selection entropy increases by >0.2 bits (indicates unexpected diversification).
  - KV hit ratio drop >= 7% sustained for 3 consecutive runs.
- Secondary checks (contextual):
  - GPU memory footprint growth >5% per minute during steady state.
  - Background OS interrupts spiking (sysstat).
- Alerting: generate a regression bundle (baseline vs current plots, deltas, artifacts) and attach to JIRA-ENG-4237 when automatic thresholds hit.

Statistical notes:
- We prefer non-parametric tests due to long-tail latency distributions. For small sample sizes (n<8) require at least 20% effect size before auto-flagging. For larger samples use bootstrap CI and Mann-Whitney.
- For change-point detection in long-running regression runs use CUSUM with tuned threshold (alpha=0.01) and minimum shift=5%.

Instrumentation and tracing fields (what we capture):
- request_id, session_id, model_variant, sequence_length, batch_size, kernel_id, kernel_duration_ms, kv_lookup_key, kv_hit_bool, kv_lookup_duration_ms, pack_time_ms, unpack_time_ms, gpu_util_percent, free_mem_bytes, timestamp_iso.
- Additionally: perf counters (l2_misses, sm_efficiency), and occasional nvprof symbol mappings for offline analysis.

Quickstart (example):
- Generate workload: python trace-synth/generate.py --seed 42 --profile small-chat --out workload-v1.json
- Start harness: ./harnessctl run --workload workload-v1.json --model-config cfg/resnet-like/q4-config.json --trace-socket /tmp/trace.sock --outdir /tmp/run-2024-11-12
- Collect: ./harnessctl collect --run /tmp/run-2024-11-12 --upload perf-store://runs/2024-11-12/kernel-probe 

Example inspection command (local):
- jq '.measurements[] | {kernel_id, p50, p95, kv_hit_ratio}' /tmp/run-2024-11-12/summary.json

Known pitfalls and mitigations:
- Non-deterministic GPU kernels: pin model to specific quantization kernel; maintain kernel fingerprint mapping so we can ignore expected kernel replacements during new driver upgrades.
- KV state drift between runs: use workload manifests that include explicit seed and initial keyspace snapshot; harnessctl will snapshot and restore KV state when requested.
- Host noise: run on perf lane nodes with isolation (systemd-run --scope) and check dmesg for OOM/power events.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- How sensitive is kernel selection to small sequence-length perturbations? Plan: sweep sequence_length around model tokenizer bucket edges and compute selection probability.
- Can we compress trace-synth manifests with a generative model to create longer realistic sessions with fewer seeds? (idea: train an LSTM on sanitized traces and sample)
- Explore adaptive sampling: under heavy KV churn, trigger heavier trace sampling for the first 30s of a run to better characterize transient behavior.

Runbook snippets (when regression found):
1) Reproduce locally with exact baseline artifacts: harnessctl run --workload reproducer.json --baseline baseline.tar.gz
2) Compare kernel selection heatmaps: tools/heatmap-compare baseline/summary.json current/summary.json
3) If kernel selection shifted, check PATCH notes in PRs touching kernel registry; if no PR, bisect recent driver/kernel updates on perf nodes.

Todo backlog (near-term):
- [ ] Add a microprobe that emulates multi-tenant KV interference (ticket JIRA-ENG-4302).
- [ ] Implement automated baseline update policy (keep most recent stable run per model/quant profile).
- [ ] Add synthetic adversarial traces (prefix collision attacks) to surface worst-case KV behavior.
- [ ] Wire harnessctl results into console/perf dashboard and add diff view per kernel_id.

References & pointers:
- Existing trace synthesis primer: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/trace-synthesis-proto
- Kernel registry: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/main/kernels
- Perf dashboard examples: perf-store://dashboards/kernel-selection-history

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intended to be iterative; please add experiments or knobs you want synthesised as issues under JIRA-ENG-4237.
- Prefer short reproducible workloads rather than very long runs for CI gating; long stability runs belong to nightly perf lanes.
